longName: Export Verified Course Completions from a State Longitudinal Data System into a Learner's Wallet
scope: One SLDS issuing course-completion LERs to one learner's wallet. PROPOSED — the issue states no scope, and see the batch/single-learner tension below.

keyConcepts.definition: State Longitudinal Data System — the state's system of record for verified student course completions and other administrative education records.

The three-party structure of verifiable-credential exchange: an Issuer who asserts, a Holder who keeps and presents, and a Verifier who checks — supported by registries that supply identity, skill definitions, and trust signals.

openIssues: A QUESTION OF ALTITUDE — the most interesting thing this rendering raises. The Introduction describes a state system that 'exports verified course completions' — plural learners, plural records, a batch — which reads as summary level. The eight shared units it inherits describe issuing ONE credential to ONE Holder, which is user-goal level. Either reading is defensible: a user-goal case invoked many times by a batch parent, or a summary case that INCLUDES the user-goal one. It is rendered as user-goal, matching the units it actually reuses, and the batch parent is left unauthored rather than guessed at. This is precisely the situation the still-open sub-case-invocation proposal exists to model, so the case is doing useful work for the standard by raising it.
No trigger is stated; the value below is PROPOSED from the Introduction narrative and awaits author confirmation.

The issue's stated benefit — 'without manual transcript requests' — implies an as-is process being displaced, which no precondition or value driver in the source names. The driver below is PROPOSED as a starting point.

Ten cited CEDS rows carry 'undefined' in both definition and URL — a familiar artifact of a template being filled in for the first time. Five resolve by name against the DME; the Credential Condition Profile / Option / Option-Component family (six rows, shared with issue #4) does not, and is carried as OrphanElements pending a look by the standards team.

An opportunity rather than a defect: nothing in this case yet cites a course, course completion, or academic record element, though course completion is its subject matter. The inherited Subject grounds the credential rather than the completion. CEDS has course and course-section classes this case could usefully cite in a second pass.

actors.role: A State Longitudinal Data System, exporting verified course completions as credentials into learners' wallets.
actors.interest: State-held administrative records become portable without staff-mediated transcript requests.

actors.role: A learner receiving, reviewing, and storing verified course-completion records.
actors.interest: I hold my own verified course record and need not request a transcript to prove it.

actors.role: Provides identity verification binding the state record to the right learner.
actors.interest: Identity assertions it supplies are relied upon correctly.

actors.role: Provides skill definitions and their metadata, addressable by globally unique URI.
actors.interest: Credentials cite registered skill definitions rather than free text.

actors.role: Publishes the Issuer's DID and public key as a trust signal.
actors.interest: Verifiers can later confirm the state's signature.

interestedParties.interest: Can accept a verified course completion directly, without a transcript-request cycle.
Records released from the SLDS are accurate, authorized, and auditable.

triggeredBy.name: SLDS verifies a course completion and the learner is eligible for credential export

assumes.statement: The course completion is verified in the state system of record and the learner is authorized to receive it as a portable credential.

condition.statement: The exported credential asserts no more than the state system of record already holds as verified.

valueDriver.title: Eliminate staff-mediated transcript requests
valueDriver.motivation: Administrative records move to the learner automatically rather than on request through institutional staff time.

scenario.condition: the Holder does not recognize the claims as their own
